title: Deeper/broader parser-lineage and cross-kernel evidence refresh
mode: primary-source web research and read-only local plan reconciliation
scope: Re-screen newly surfaced DWG/DXF viewers and wrappers for parser lineage
Audit field-specific cross-reference claims in the ft_model DWG implementation notes
Separate renderer/application evidence from parser and kernel evidence
Reconcile recent cross-backend topology-matching research with existing semantic validation gates

method.kind: Read current project documentation/source pages and a research preprint; reconcile evidence classes with the existing plan
method.limitations: Findings are based on mutable repository documentation/source pages and a preprint, not pinned or executed peer artifacts. The exact ft_model binaries, DWG corpus, current CI outputs, ProGPU SAT/SAB implementation, and consumer renderings were not built or run. No claim is made about code copying; the ft_model documentation explicitly cross-references LibreDWG for selected algorithm decisions, so those fields are not independent corroboration.

sources.observed: The project describes an MIT C++20 DWG/DXF-to-scene/2D-rendering route. Its PROJECT_STATUS describes version-specific gaps and historical entity comparison rates, and explicitly attributes the R2004 object-map accumulator behavior to LibreDWG's read_2004_section_handles. Accordingly, its implementation is diverse but not an independent source for the specifically cross-referenced object-map decision. No exact reproducible public real-DWG input manifest/run receipt was bound in this pass.

The reviewed projects document DWG routes through LibreDWG/WASM or dwg2dxf, with distinct DXF and rendering layers. Their UI/adapter/rendering behavior may be consumer evidence, but the DWG parse path is not a new independent implementation lineage.

sources.revision: Mutable project architecture, DXF note, and README reviewed 2026-10-18
sources.observed: The active ProGPU CAD architecture identifies ACadSharp as its file-format model; the older ProGPU.Dxf route remains a legacy/migration component. ProCad likewise describes ACadSharp-backed DWG/DXF I/O. Their application/rendering route is not an independent DWG/DXF parser or B-rep kernel witness.

The paper describes an OCCT/OCP-backed editable modeling IR and Geometric Signature Matching for face/edge correspondence across backend changes. It is not a DWG/DXF parser, ACIS grammar reference, normative shape-equivalence procedure, or independent ACIS/AcDs semantic result.

assessment.planImpact: Refines existing PAR-07/S8 parser-lineage and consumer evidence, PAR-11 expected-value provenance, and the composed semantic gate. Distinguish implementation diversity from independent algorithm evidence; treat wrappers as adapter/consumer routes; keep topology correspondence as a diagnostic or declared identity-preserving check rather than a universal semantic requirement. No new peer run enters the fast slice loop.

implementationReadyChecks: For each optional peer, capture implementation relation, specification/source relation, expected-value origin, consumer/kernel relation, and exact artifact/run identity; do not compress these into one independence flag.
For ft_model, do not count LibreDWG-referenced object-map or CMC decisions as a second independent vote; require an exact source/build and available hash-bound inputs before any optional comparison.
For viewer wrappers, identify the actual converter/parser selected for the run and report wrapper/render behavior separately from parser behavior.

If CADIR-style topology matching is used, treat it as a correspondence diagnostic; semantic acceptance still requires a complete valid body, independent expected geometry/operation, and explicit tolerances.
When source, artifact, input, or independent expected manifest is unavailable, record NOT_RUN and continue local work; no optional peer is a per-slice prerequisite.
Keep the existing fast implementation loop and composed-only peer/native checks; do not add fixtures, dependencies, tests, or validation frequency from this research alone.
